definition_zh: 可供替代的；非传统的；替代方案；选择
definition_en: another possibility instead of the usual one, or a choice between two or more things
core_image: 岔路口立着两块路牌，一块指向老路，一块指向新路
scene: 医生建议先休息，如果还疼再考虑别的方案，比如物理治疗。The doctor suggested an alternative treatment.
sceneCN: 这里 alternative 是「可供替代的」（第 1 个义项：在常规办法之外另有一种可选做法）；句意是医生建议了一种替代疗法。

pos.zh: 形容词：可供替代的；非传统的

derivatives.zh: 副词：或者；作为另一种选择
动词：改变，与 alternative 同源

senses.title: Another possible choice
senses.titleCN: 可供替代的；另一可选的
senses.definition: available as another possibility in place of the usual or first one
senses.definitionCN: 作为常规或首选之外的另一可能而存在
senses.example: We need an alternative route because the bridge is closed.
senses.exampleCN: 桥封了，我们需要另一条路线。
senses.why: The Latin base alter means 'the other of two', and -native makes an adjective of offering, so alternative describes what stands ready as the other choice.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基 alter 意为「两者中的另一个」，-native 构成表示「提供」的形容词，所以 alternative 指作为另一个选择随时可用的方案。

senses.title: Outside the mainstream
senses.definition: deliberately different from the dominant or conventional system, as in alternative medicine or energy
senses.definitionCN: 有意区别于主流或传统体系，如替代医学、替代能源
senses.example: Some patients turn to alternative medicine when drugs fail.
senses.exampleCN: 有些病人在药物无效时转向替代疗法。
senses.why: Twentieth-century counterculture gave the word a second edge: the alternative is not merely another option but a rejection of the established one.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪的反主流文化给这个词添了第二层锋芒：alternative 不只是另一个选项，还带有对既定做法的拒绝。

senses.title: A choice to be made
senses.definition: one of two or more things that can be chosen, especially when the first is unsatisfactory
senses.definitionCN: 两个或多个可选事物之一，尤指首选不理想时的备选
senses.example: The committee saw no alternative but to cancel the event.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会别无选择，只能取消活动。
senses.why: As a noun the word names the second path itself, and the common phrase no alternative shows how it carries the weight of a forced decision.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时，这个词指第二条路本身，常见说法 no alternative 正体现它承载着「被迫决断」的分量。

intro.en: Alternative is built on the Latin idea of 'the other of two', later widened to any option and finally to anti-mainstream choices.
intro.cn: alternative 建立在拉丁语「两者中的另一个」之上，后来扩为任何选项，最终又指反主流的选择。

items.en: alter meant 'the other of two', the root also seen in alter ego.
items.cn: alter 意为「两者中的另一个」，也见于 alter ego。

items.en: alternare meant 'to do one thing then the other, to alternate'.
items.cn: alternare 意为「轮流做一件事和另一件事」。

items.en: French formed alternatif for a choice that offers one thing or the other.
items.cn: 法语构成 alternatif，指非此即彼的选择。

items.en: English alternative first described a choice between two possibilities.
items.cn: 英语 alternative 最初描述两种可能之间的取舍。

items.en: The modern sense of alternative energy or medicine marks a deliberate move away from the mainstream.
items.cn: 二十世纪出现的 alternative energy、alternative medicine 表示有意离开主流。

note.en: The look-alike group separates alter, alternate, and alternative; the near-meaning group names kinds of options.
note.cn: 形近组区分 alter、alternate 与 alternative；近义组列出各类选项。

definition_zh: 海拔；高度；（几何中的）高
definition_en: the height of a place above sea level, height in general, or the perpendicular height of a geometric figure
core_image: 飞机舷窗外的雪山，仪表盘上标着飞行高度
scene: 飞机爬升到巡航高度后，窗外的河流变成了一条细线。The plane reached a cruising altitude of ten thousand metres.
sceneCN: 这里 altitude 是「高度」（第 2 个义项：物体离地面的垂直距离）；句意是飞机达到了一万米的巡航高度。

derivatives.zh: 名词：高原，与 altitude 同源于「高」
名词：中音；高音，源自拉丁语「高」

senses.title: Height above sea level
senses.definition: the vertical distance of a place above the level of the sea, used in geography and travel
senses.definitionCN: 某地高出海平面的垂直距离，用于地理与旅行
senses.example: The village sits at an altitude of three thousand metres.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村庄位于海拔三千米处。
senses.why: Latin altitudo came from altus, 'high', and in geography the word was fixed to the one reference line that matters, the sea.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 altitudo 来自 altus「高的」，在地理中这个词被固定到唯一重要的基准线，也就是海平面。

senses.title: Height above the ground
senses.definition: the height of an aircraft or object above the ground or a chosen level at a particular moment
senses.definitionCN: 飞机或物体在某一时刻离地面或某一基准的高度
senses.example: The plane reached a cruising altitude of ten thousand metres.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机达到了一万米的巡航高度。
senses.why: Once the word meant height in general, aviation could use it for a changing measurement rather than a fixed spot on the map.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本泛指高度，航空便用它表示不断变化的测量值，而不是地图上固定的地点。

senses.title: Perpendicular height of a figure
senses.definition: the line drawn at right angles from a vertex to the opposite side of a triangle or solid
senses.definitionCN: 从顶点垂直画到对边的线段，用于三角形或立体图形
senses.example: The area of a triangle is half the base times the altitude.
senses.exampleCN: 三角形的面积等于底乘高的一半。
senses.why: Geometry kept the pure sense of 'height' and gave it a precise meaning: the perpendicular distance from a vertex to the opposite side.
senses.whyCN: 几何学保留了「高度」的纯粹含义，并给它精确定义：从顶点到对边的垂直距离。

intro.en: Altitude descends from the Latin word for height and was later borrowed by geography, aviation, and geometry.
intro.cn: altitude 源自拉丁语表示「高度」的词，后来被地理、航空与几何分别借用。

items.en: altus meant 'high, deep', and it also underlies alto and altimeter.
items.cn: altus 意为「高的、深的」，也是 alto 与 altimeter 的来源。

items.en: altitudo was the abstract noun for height or depth.
items.cn: altitudo 是表示高度或深度的抽象名词。

items.en: French passed the word into English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 法语在十四世纪把这个词传入英语。

items.en: Mapmakers fixed altitude to height above sea level.
items.cn: 地图绘制者把 altitude 固定为高出海平面的高度。

items.en: Flight added the sense of an aircraft's height at a given moment.
items.cn: 航空又增添了飞机在某一时刻的高度的含义。

items.en: Mathematicians used altitude for the perpendicular height of a figure.
items.cn: 数学家用 altitude 指图形的垂直高。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one syllable; the near-meaning group separates height and elevation.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个音节；近义组区分高度与海拔。

definition_zh: n. 女低音；女低音歌手；中音乐器（如中音萨克斯）
definition_en: The lowest adult female singing voice, a singer who takes that line, or an instrument whose range matches it, such as an alto saxophone.
core_image: 合唱里托在主旋律下方的那一层声音
scene: 合唱团缺了中间那一层，排练时和声总是空着。The choir needs one more alto before Friday.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：合唱团里唱女低音声部的那个人。指挥说周五之前还要再招一位，否则中间那层和声一直空着。

pos.zh: 女低音；女低音歌手；中音乐器

senses.title: The low female line
senses.titleCN: 女低音声部；女低音歌手
senses.definition: the lowest adult female singing voice, or a singer who performs that part in a choir
senses.definitionCN: 成年女性最低的歌唱声部，或在合唱团中演唱该声部的歌手
senses.example: She moved from soprano to alto after her voice settled.
senses.exampleCN: 嗓音定型后，她从女高音转到女低音。
senses.why: Italian alto meant high, because the line was once the high part sung by men above the tenor; when women took it over, the same name came to mean the lowest female line.
senses.whyCN: 意大利语 alto 意为「高」，因为这条旋律线曾是男声在男高音之上唱的高声部；女性接手后，同一个名称就转而指最低的女声线。

senses.title: An instrument of that range
senses.definition: an instrument built to cover the same range as that voice, as in an alto saxophone or alto flute
senses.definitionCN: 音域与该人声声部相当的乐器，如中音萨克斯或中音长笛
senses.example: He bought a second-hand alto for the school band.
senses.exampleCN: 他为学校乐队买了一把二手中音萨克斯。
senses.why: Instruments are labelled by the voice range they replace, so alto travels from the choir stall to the brass shelf without changing its meaning.
senses.whyCN: 乐器按其替代的人声音域标注，因此 alto 从合唱席位走到铜管乐器架上，含义并未改变。

intro.en: Alto is Italian for high, from Latin altus, which in turn comes from alere, to nourish. The name stayed the same while the range it described moved from a high male part to the lowest female one.
intro.cn: alto 是意大利语的「高」，来自拉丁语 altus，而 altus 又来自 alere「滋养」。名称一直没变，它所描述的音域却从男声的高声部移到了最低的女声部。

items.en: Latin altus meant high or tall, and originally grown or nourished, from the verb alere, to feed and bring up. Height was pictured as the result of being fed.
items.cn: 拉丁语 altus 意为「高的、高的」，最初指「长成的、被养育的」，来自动词 alere「喂养、养育」。高度被想象为被喂养的结果。

items.en: Italian kept alto for high. In church music the alto line sat above the tenor and was sung by men, so the part was genuinely the high one.
items.cn: 意大利语保留 alto 表示「高」。在教堂音乐中，alto 声部位于男高音之上，由男声演唱，因此那确实是高声部。

items.en: English took alto in the eighteenth century as a musical term for that male high part, along with the Italian vocabulary of tempo and dynamics.
items.cn: 英语在 18 世纪把 alto 作为音乐术语借入，指那个男声高声部，同时借入的还有意大利语的速度与力度词汇。

items.en: When women replaced the male singers, the line sounded an octave lower in absolute terms, and alto came to name the lowest female voice. The label kept its old shape.
items.cn: 当女性取代男歌手后，这条线在绝对音高上低了一个八度，alto 于是转指最低的女声。标签保留了旧的样子。

items.en: Modern English uses alto for the voice, the singer and instruments of that range, while the same Latin altus survives in altitude and altimeter.
items.cn: 现代英语用 alto 指声部、歌手以及该音域的乐器，而同一个拉丁语 altus 仍保存在 altitude 与 altimeter 中。

note.cn: 形近组先把 alto 与 altar、alter 分开，再保留 alt-「高」词族；近义组列出相邻的声部名称。

senses.exampleCN: 她这个利他的选择让她损失了一年的积蓄。
senses.why: The base is Latin alter, the other of two, so the word literally points away from the self and toward the other person.
senses.whyCN: 词根是拉丁语 alter「两者中的另一个」，所以这个词字面上就把手从自己指向了他人。

senses.title: In biology and ethics
senses.titleCN: 生物学与伦理学中的利他
senses.definition: describing behaviour that lowers the fitness or payoff of the actor while raising that of another
senses.definitionCN: 用于描述降低行动者自身适合度或收益、却提高他人收益的行为
senses.example: Altruistic grooming is common among related bats.
senses.exampleCN: 利他性的相互梳理在亲缘蝙蝠中很常见。
senses.why: Comte coined the noun as the opposite of egoism, and the sciences kept that strict sense: a real cost to the giver, a real gain to the receiver.
senses.whyCN: 孔德把这个名词造出来作为利己主义的反面，各门学科保留了这一严格含义：给予者确有损失，接受者确有收益。

intro.en: Altruistic is the adjective of altruism, a word Auguste Comte coined in French around 1830 from autrui, other people, which descends from Latin alter, the other of two.
intro.cn: altruistic 是 altruism 的形容词，而 altruism 是孔德约 1830 年在法语中造的词，来自 autrui「他人」，后者又源自拉丁语 alter「两者中的另一个」。

items.en: Latin alter meant the other of two. It is the base of the whole family: alternate, alternative and the phrase alter ego.
items.cn: 拉丁语 alter 意为「两者中的另一个」。它是整个词族的底座：alternate、alternative 以及短语 alter ego。

items.en: Old French autrui, other people, grew out of a Latin form built on alter, with the l turning into a u sound on the way.
items.cn: 古法语 autrui「他人」由建立在 alter 之上的拉丁语形式发展而来，途中 l 变成了 u 音。

items.en: Auguste Comte coined French altruisme around 1830 from autrui, pairing it against egoisme to name the principle of living for others.
items.cn: 孔德约 1830 年由 autrui 造出法语 altruisme，与 egoisme 相对，用来命名「为他人而活」的原则。

items.en: English took altruism in the mid nineteenth century, and George Henry Lewes spread it through his writing on Comte and positivism.
items.cn: 英语在 19 世纪中期借入 altruism，刘易斯通过介绍孔德与实证主义的著作把它推广开来。

items.en: Altruistic is the adjective built with -istic, now standard in ethics, psychology, evolutionary biology and ordinary praise of a generous act.
items.cn: altruistic 是用 -istic 构成的形容词，如今在伦理学、心理学、演化生物学以及对慷慨行为的日常称赞中都是标准用词。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the altru- family and the -istic ending; the near-meaning group lists other words for putting others first.
note.cn: 形近组保留 altru- 词族与 -istic 词尾；近义组列出其他表示「把他人放在前面」的词。

normalIntro.en: Altruistic hides alter, the other: the word literally turns you toward the other person.
normalIntro.cn: altruistic 里藏着 alter「他人」：这个词字面上就是把你转向另一个人。

normal.en: Alter means other, so altruistic means other-first.
normal.cn: alter 意为「他人」，所以 altruistic 就是「他人优先」。

normal.en: It is the opposite of egoistic, and Comte designed the pair.
normal.cn: 它是 egoistic 的反面，这一对是孔德有意设计的。

normal.en: Use more altruistic, not altruisticer: the word is too long for -er.
normal.cn: 用 more altruistic，不用 altruisticer：这个词太长，不加 -er。

normal.en: The noun is altruism, the person is an altruist.
normal.cn: 名词是 altruism，人是 altruist。

normal.en: Do not confuse altruistic with authentic: one is about others, one about truth.
normal.cn: 别把 altruistic 与 authentic 混淆：一个讲他人，一个讲真实。

abstract.cn: 想象有人把桌边最后一把椅子推给陌生人。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand giving away the whole loaf and keeping the crumbs.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把整条面包送出去，只留下碎屑。

abstract.cn: 想象一只蝙蝠为再也见不到的表亲梳理毛发。

examples.en: His altruistic motives were never in doubt.
examples.cn: 他的利他动机从未受到怀疑。

examples.en: The donation was purely altruistic, with no tax benefit.
examples.cn: 这笔捐赠纯粹是利他的，没有任何税收好处。

examples.en: She acted altruistically and asked for nothing back.
examples.cn: 她无私地行事，不求任何回报。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱他如实」——爱他（altru）如实（istic）：实实在在地爱别人、不图回报，就是利他的、无私的。

root: 拉丁语 alter「两者中的另一个」经古法语 autrui「他人」，由孔德造出 altruisme，英语借为 altruism「利他主义」，再加 -istic 构成形容词 altruistic，字面即「把他人放在自己之前」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the same outward turn: everyday praise for a generous motive, and the technical label for behaviour that costs the giver.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一次向外的转身：日常里对慷慨动机的称赞，以及学术上对「给予者付出代价」的行为的标注。

intro.cn: altruistic 是 alter 加 -ism 加 -ist 加 -istic，这条链把「他人」变成了对品格的描述。

latinIntro.en: Latin alter, the other of two, became Old French autrui; Comte built altruisme on it and English added the adjective ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 alter「两者中的另一个」变成古法语 autrui；孔德在其上造出 altruisme，英语再加形容词词尾。

definition_zh: 铝；铝材
definition_en: a light silvery metal that does not rust easily, used for cans, foil, and aircraft parts
core_image: 一卷银亮的铝箔在厨房台面上展开
scene: 厨房里，她把剩菜用铝箔包好，放进冰箱。She wrapped the leftovers in aluminium foil.
sceneCN: 这里 aluminium 是「铝」（第 1 个义项：一种轻而耐锈的银白色金属）；句意是她用铝箔把剩菜包好。

senses.title: The metal element
senses.definition: the chemical element of atomic number thirteen, a light silvery metal that resists corrosion
senses.definitionCN: 原子序数为十三的化学元素，是轻质银白色且耐腐蚀的金属
senses.example: Aluminium is extracted from bauxite by electrolysis.
senses.exampleCN: 铝通过电解从铝土矿中提炼出来。
senses.why: The name comes from Latin alumen, 'alum', the mineral from which the metal was first isolated, so the word begins as a chemical label.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字来自拉丁语 alumen「明矾」，即最早分离出该金属的矿物，所以这个词起初是化学名称。

senses.title: The metal as a material
senses.definition: the metal considered as an everyday manufacturing material, as in foil, cans, and frames
senses.definitionCN: 把这种金属当作日常制造材料来用，如铝箔、铝罐与框架
senses.example: The window frames are made of aluminium, not steel.
senses.exampleCN: 窗框是铝制的，不是钢的。
senses.why: Because the metal is light and does not rust, industry talks about aluminium as a material to be shaped, which is why it appears in foil, cans, and aircraft.
senses.whyCN: 因为这种金属轻且不生锈，工业界把它当作可加工的材料来谈，因此它出现在铝箔、铝罐与飞机部件中。

intro.en: Aluminium is a modern scientific name built on the Latin word for alum.
intro.cn: aluminium 是建立在拉丁语「明矾」一词上的现代科学名称。

items.en: alumen meant 'alum', the mineral salt used in dyeing and medicine.
items.cn: alumen 意为「明矾」，是用于染色与医药的矿物盐。

items.en: English kept alum for the mineral, the source of the metal's name.
items.cn: 英语以 alum 保留了这个矿物名，它正是金属名称的来源。

items.en: Humphry Davy proposed aluminum for the newly isolated metal.
items.cn: 汉弗莱·戴维在 1808 年为新分离出的金属提出 aluminum 这一名称。

items.en: Writers adopted aluminium to match other elements ending in -ium.
items.cn: 人们采用 aluminium，以与其他以 -ium 结尾的元素名一致。

items.en: American English kept Davy's aluminum, while British English kept aluminium.
items.cn: 美式英语沿用戴维的 aluminum，英式英语则用 aluminium。

note.en: The look-alike group covers the spellings and the ore; the near-meaning group places it among metals.
note.cn: 形近组涵盖拼写与矿石；近义组把它放进金属类别。

sensesIntro.cn: 同一种金属有两个侧面：化学元素与工业材料。

latinIntro.cn: 词基 alumen 属拉丁语，后缀沿用元素命名的模式。

definition_zh: n. 女校友；女毕业生（复数 alumnae）
definition_en: A female former student or graduate of a school, college or university; the plural form is alumnae.
core_image: 毕业多年后仍被母校叫作「养女」的那个人
scene: 她毕业二十年，每年校庆都坐在第一排。The college honoured its oldest alumna at the ceremony.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：她是从这所学院毕业的女性，所以用 alumna 而不是 alumnus。校方在校庆上向这位最年长的女校友致敬。

senses.title: A female graduate
senses.definition: a woman who formerly studied at a particular school, college or university
senses.definitionCN: 曾在某所学校、学院或大学就读的女性
senses.example: She is an alumna of the medical school.
senses.exampleCN: 她是这所医学院的女校友。
senses.why: Latin alumnus meant a foster child or pupil, one nourished by a household; the -a ending marks the feminine, so the school is still pictured as a foster mother.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 alumnus 意为养子或学生，即被一个家庭养育的人；-a 词尾标示阴性，因此学校仍被想象为养母。

senses.title: In institutional records
senses.definition: used by colleges in titles, lists and fundraising to identify women on the graduate roll
senses.definitionCN: 高校在头衔、名录与募捐中用以标识毕业生名册上的女性
senses.example: The alumnae fund paid for two new scholarships.
senses.exampleCN: 女校友基金资助了两项新奖学金。
senses.why: Institutions keep the Latin plurals because their rolls are formal documents, so alumnae appears where speech would simply say alums.
senses.whyCN: 院校保留拉丁语复数，因为名录属于正式文件，所以在口语只说 alums 的地方，书面仍写 alumnae。

intro.en: Alumna is the feminine of Latin alumnus, a foster child or pupil, from alere, to nourish. The school is imagined as the household that fed you, and the ending tells the gender.
intro.cn: alumna 是拉丁语 alumnus 的阴性形式，alumnus 意为养子或学生，来自 alere「滋养」。学校被想象为喂养过你的那个家，词尾则标示性别。

items.en: Latin alere meant to nourish, feed or bring up. The same root gives aliment, alimentary and, through altus, altitude.
items.cn: 拉丁语 alere 意为「滋养、喂养、养育」。同一词根产生 aliment、alimentary，并经 altus 产生 altitude。

items.en: Alumnus was the noun for a foster son or pupil, literally one who is nourished. A teacher or a school stood in the place of a parent.
items.cn: alumnus 是表示养子或学生的名词，字面为「被养育的人」。老师或学校站在父母的位置上。

items.en: Alumna is the feminine singular and alumnae the feminine plural, while alumnus and alumni are the masculine pair. English borrowed all four intact.
items.cn: alumna 是阴性单数，alumnae 是阴性复数，而 alumnus 与 alumni 是阳性的一对。英语把四个形式整套借入。

items.en: English took alumnus in the seventeenth century and alumna later, as women began to keep their own graduate rolls at colleges.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪借入 alumnus，alumna 较晚，随着女性开始在高校拥有自己的毕业生名册而通行。

items.en: Today alum serves for any gender in speech, while formal writing still separates alumna, alumnae, alumnus and alumni.
items.cn: 如今口语中 alum 不分性别通用，而正式书面语仍区分 alumna、alumnae、alumnus 与 alumni。

examples.cn: 女校友们聚集在旧图书馆里。

examples.en: She is a proud alumna of a small state college.

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is alere, to nourish, giving alumnus and its feminine alumna; alma, nourishing, survives in alma mater.

senses.definitionCN: 曾在某所学校、学院或大学就读的男性
senses.example: He is an alumnus of the engineering faculty.
senses.exampleCN: 他是工学院的校友。
senses.why: Latin alumnus meant a foster son, one nourished by a household, so the word carries the idea that the school fed your mind and you still owe it something.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 alumnus 意为养子，即被一个家庭养育的人，因此这个词带着「学校喂养过你的头脑、你仍欠它一份情」的意味。

senses.title: The mixed plural
senses.definition: used in the plural alumni for a body of former students of any gender
senses.definitionCN: 以复数 alumni 指任何性别构成的毕业生群体
senses.example: The alumni voted to fund a new laboratory.
senses.exampleCN: 校友们投票决定资助一间新实验室。
senses.why: Latin used the masculine plural for a mixed group, and English campus practice kept that rule, which is why alumni covers everyone while alumnae does not.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语用阳性复数指混合群体，英语校园沿用了这一规则，所以 alumni 涵盖所有人，而 alumnae 不涵盖。

intro.en: Alumnus is Latin for a foster son or pupil, from alere, to nourish. English kept the Latin plural alumni, and that plural is now the everyday word for a whole graduate body.
intro.cn: alumnus 在拉丁语中意为养子或学生，来自 alere「滋养」。英语保留了拉丁语复数 alumni，而这个复数如今就是「全体毕业生」的日常说法。

items.en: Alere meant to feed, nourish or bring up. From it come aliment, alimentary and alumnus, all built on the idea of being fed.
items.cn: alere 意为「喂养、滋养、养育」。由它产生 aliment、alimentary 与 alumnus，都建立在「被喂养」这个想法上。

items.en: Alumnus named a foster child raised in someone else house, and by extension a pupil raised by a teacher. The relation is one of care, not of blood.
items.cn: alumnus 指在别人家中养大的孩子，引申为由老师带大的学生。这种关系是养育关系，不是血缘关系。

items.en: The plural alumni covered a group of male or mixed pupils. English kept the form and widened it to the whole graduate body of an institution.
items.cn: 复数 alumni 指一群男性或混合性别的学生。英语保留该形式，并把它扩大到一所机构的全部毕业生。

items.en: American colleges organised alumni associations and alumni funds in the nineteenth century, which made the plural far more common than the singular.
items.cn: 美国高校在 19 世纪组织校友会与校友基金，这使复数形式远比单数常见。

items.en: Modern English uses alumnus for one man, alumni for a group, and the clipped alum in speech when gender does not matter.
items.cn: 现代英语用 alumnus 指一位男性，alumni 指一个群体，口语中在性别无关紧要时用缩写 alum。

note.en: The look-alike group sets the four Latin forms side by side; the near-meaning group lists other campus words for someone who has left.
note.cn: 形近组把四个拉丁语形式并排；近义组列出校园里其他表示「已离校者」的词。

normalIntro.cn: alumnus 以 -us 结尾，这是拉丁语阳性词尾，复数把 -us 换成 -i。

normal.cn: 词根意为「滋养」：学校喂养过你，所以你是它的 alumnus。

normal.en: Alumni is the plural you will meet most often in newsletters.
normal.cn: alumni 是你在校讯里最常见到的复数。

normal.en: Alumni can cover a mixed group; alumnae cannot.
normal.cn: alumni 可以指混合群体，alumnae 不行。

normal.en: Alma mater is the nourishing mother, the same al- root.
normal.cn: alma mater 是「滋养的母亲」，同一个 al- 词根。

normal.en: Do not write alumnus for a woman; that is alumna.

abstract.cn: 想象一个成年男子走回一间小教室。

abstract.en: Imagine a school sending a bill of gratitude instead of fees.
abstract.cn: 想象学校寄来的不是学费单，而是一份感激清单。

abstract.en: Think of a crowd of former pupils filling one hall.
abstract.cn: 想象一群旧日学生挤满一个礼堂。

examples.cn: 这所大学把每位校友都视为家庭的一员。

examples.en: Alumni from fifty years ago still meet each spring.
examples.cn: 五十年前的校友每年春天仍会聚会。

examples.en: He remained a generous alumnus long after retirement.
examples.cn: 退休很久之后，他仍是一位慷慨的校友。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the same nourishing tie: one man who was fed here, and the whole body of people who were.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一条养育纽带：一个曾在此被喂养的人，以及所有曾被喂养的人构成的整体。

definition_zh: n. 混合物；混合体；汞合金（尤指补牙用的银汞合金）
definition_en: A mixture or blend of different elements; also an alloy of mercury with another metal, especially the paste used in dental fillings.
core_image: 几种不同的东西被揉成看不出原样的一团
scene: 这家餐馆把川菜和粤菜混在一起，味道反倒很协调。The menu is an amalgam of two regional styles.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：菜单不是单一菜系，而是两种地方风格揉在一起的混合体。这正是 amalgam 的引申用法。

senses.title: A blend of different things
senses.definition: a thing made by combining several different elements so that they no longer stand apart
senses.definitionCN: 把若干不同成分结合起来、使它们不再各自分立而成的东西
senses.example: The film is an amalgam of comedy and grief.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影是喜剧与悲伤的混合体。
senses.why: The word began as a soft metallic paste that could be worked by hand, so the image is of separate pieces kneaded into one mass.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指可用手揉捏的软金属膏，所以意象是把分散的碎块揉成一团。

senses.title: A mercury alloy
senses.definition: an alloy of mercury with another metal, especially the silver paste used to fill teeth
senses.definitionCN: 汞与另一种金属形成的合金，尤指用于补牙的银汞膏
senses.example: The dentist replaced the old amalgam with resin.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医用树脂替换了旧的银汞合金。
senses.why: Alchemists needed a metal that stayed soft enough to shape, and mercury supplied it; the technical sense is the older one.
senses.whyCN: 炼金术士需要一种保持柔软、便于塑形的金属，汞提供了这一点；技术义是更古老的那个义项。

intro.en: Amalgam comes from Greek malagma, a softening poultice, through Arabic al-malgham and Medieval Latin amalgama. The soft paste of the workshop became any blend at all.
intro.cn: amalgam 来自希腊语 malagma「软化膏」，经阿拉伯语 al-malgham 与中世纪拉丁语 amalgama 而来。作坊里的软膏后来变成泛指任何混合物。

items.en: Greek malagma meant a softening poultice, from malassein, to soften. The base idea is a soft mass worked by hand until it spreads.
items.cn: 希腊语 malagma 意为「软化用的膏药」，来自 malassein「使变软」。基本想法是一团用手揉到能摊开的软物质。

items.en: Arabic al-malgham carried the term into alchemy for a soft paste of mercury mixed with another metal.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 al-malgham 把这个词带入炼金术，指汞与另一种金属混成的软膏。

items.en: Medieval Latin amalgama appears in alchemical texts of the thirteenth century, keeping the sense of a workable metallic paste.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 amalgama 见于 13 世纪的炼金术文献，保留「可加工的金属膏」这一含义。

items.en: Old French amalgame passed the word into English in the fifteenth century, still mainly a term of the metal workshop.
items.cn: 古法语 amalgame 在 15 世纪把该词传入英语，当时仍主要是金属作坊的术语。

items.en: From the metal paste English widened amalgam to any blend of styles or ideas, and built amalgamate and amalgamation for the act of merging.
items.cn: 英语从金属膏出发，把 amalgam 扩大到风格或思想的任何混合，并造出 amalgamate 与 amalgamation 表示合并这一动作。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the amalgam- family and one similar opening; the near-meaning group lists other words for things combined.
note.cn: 形近组保留 amalgam- 词族与一个相近开头；近义组列出其他表示「结合而成之物」的词。

abstract.en: Imagine two music styles melting into one track.
abstract.cn: 想象两种音乐风格融进同一首曲子。

abstract.en: Think of a city where every street borrowed from somewhere else.
abstract.cn: 想象一座每条街都从别处借来元素的城市。

examples.en: The book is an amalgam of diary and essay.
examples.cn: 这本书是日记与随笔的混合体。

examples.en: Dental amalgam has been used for over a century.
examples.cn: 牙科银汞合金已使用了一个多世纪。

examples.en: Two small firms formed an amalgam to survive.
examples.cn: 两家小公司合并成一个整体以求生存。

root: 希腊语 malassein「使变软」生出 malagma「软化膏」，阿拉伯语加冠词成 al-malgham，中世纪拉丁语定为 amalgama，指汞与金属揉成的软膏，引申为任何混合体。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one soft mass: the technical paste of mercury and metal, and the general blend of anything at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一团软物质：技术上是汞与金属的膏，一般义是任何东西的混合。

latinIntro.en: The base is Greek malagma, a soft poultice; Arabic added al-, and Medieval Latin fixed the form amalgama before French passed it on.

definition_zh: 积聚；积累；聚集；堆积
definition_en: to gather together or collect a large amount of something over time
core_image: 雪球越滚越大：一点一点把东西拢成一大堆
scene: 老人坐在账本前清点一生攒下的家产。Over decades he managed to amass a huge fortune.
sceneCN: 这里的 amass 是「积聚」（第 1 个义项：逐渐积累大量财富）；句意是他几十年间攒下了一大笔财富。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「积聚；聚积之物」，较少用
由 mass 加形容词后缀构成，义为「巨大的」

senses.title: To accumulate wealth over time
senses.definition: to gradually gather a large amount of money or property
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐聚集大量钱财或资产
senses.example: She amassed a fortune in the shipping trade.
senses.exampleCN: 她靠航运业积攒了一笔巨款。
senses.why: Wealth is pictured as loose coins being gathered into one great mass.
senses.whyCN: 财富被想象成散落的钱币被拢成一大堆。

senses.title: To collect a large quantity of things
senses.definition: to bring together a large number of objects or items
senses.definitionCN: 把大量物件汇集到一起
senses.example: The museum has amassed a remarkable collection of old maps.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆汇集了一大批珍贵的老地图收藏。
senses.why: The same gathering image applies to any objects piled into one place.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「聚拢」意象适用于堆在一处的任何物品。

senses.title: To gather information or evidence
senses.definition: to accumulate facts, data, or proof in quantity
senses.definitionCN: 大量积累事实、数据或证据
senses.example: Lawyers amassed enough evidence to reopen the case.
senses.exampleCN: 律师们收集到足够的证据使案件重审。
senses.why: Abstract items are treated like a pile that grows heavier piece by piece.
senses.whyCN: 抽象事物被当作一堆逐件增重的物质来对待。

senses.title: To assemble people or troops
senses.definition: to bring soldiers or crowds together in one place
senses.definitionCN: 把士兵或人群召集到一处
senses.example: The general amassed his troops on the northern border.
senses.exampleCN: 将军在北部边境集结了军队。
senses.why: A crowd, like matter, forms one dense mass when gathered.
senses.whyCN: 人群和物质一样，聚集起来便形成一个密集的群体。

senses.title: To pile up as debts or problems
senses.titleCN: 堆积（债务、问题等负面事物）
senses.definition: to accumulate something undesirable, such as debt or trouble
senses.definitionCN: 积累债务、麻烦等不良事物
senses.example: The company amassed huge debts before collapsing.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司在倒闭前积欠了巨额债务。
senses.why: The mass can be heavy in a bad way; the verb stays neutral and the context turns negative.
senses.whyCN: 「一大堆」也可以是坏的重负，动词本身中性，由语境转贬。

senses.title: To accumulate naturally or by deposit
senses.definition: to build up gradually as matter settles or collects, as with snow or dust
senses.definitionCN: 如雪、尘等物质沉降聚集而逐渐增厚
senses.example: Grey dust had amassed on the abandoned shelves.
senses.exampleCN: 废弃的书架上积了厚厚的灰尘。
senses.why: Without human agency, small particles still merge into a mass.
senses.whyCN: 无需人力，细小颗粒也会聚成一体。

senses.title: To gather knowledge or experience
senses.definition: to acquire a large store of learning or practical skill over the years
senses.definitionCN: 多年间积累大量学识或经验
senses.example: He amassed a lifetime of wisdom working in the village clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 他在乡村诊所工作中积累了一生的智慧。
senses.why: Knowledge is stored like grain in a barn, a heap added to year after year.
senses.whyCN: 知识像谷仓里的粮堆，年复一年地添高。

senses.title: To crowd together physically
senses.definition: to form a dense crowd or heap in one place
senses.definitionCN: 在一处形成密集的人群或堆
senses.example: Protesters amassed outside the city hall all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 抗议者整个上午都在市政厅外聚集。
senses.why: The intransitive use shows the mass forming by itself.
senses.whyCN: 不及物用法显示这个「团块」自行形成。

intro.en: Amass joins the Latin prefix ad- (to) with massa (lump, mass), passing through Old French into English.
intro.cn: amass 由拉丁语前缀 ad-（朝向）加 massa（团、块）构成，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: maza, "barley cake, lump", a likely relative of mass.
items.cn: 希腊语 maza「大麦饼、团块」，一般认为是 mass 的亲戚（重构形式）。

items.en: massa, "lump of dough, mass".
items.cn: 拉丁语 massa「面团；团块」。

items.en: amasser, "to gather into a mass", from a- (from ad-) plus masser.
items.cn: 古法语 amasser「聚成一团」，由 a-（来自 ad-）加 masser 构成。

items.en: English amass appears in the fifteenth century with the sense of gathering into a heap.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语 amass 出现，义为聚集成堆。

items.en: Now the standard verb for accumulating wealth, data, or forces in quantity.
items.cn: 如今是表示大量积累财富、数据或力量的标准动词。

note.en: Distinguish amass from its root mass and from near synonyms of accumulating.
note.cn: 要把 amass 与词根词 mass 以及表示积累的近义词区分开。

entries.definition: the root noun: a large body of matter or quantity.
a Greek-derived medical word sharing only the a-m spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语来源的医学词，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: adjective from mass, meaning very large and heavy.
entries.definitionCN: 由 mass 派生的形容词，义为巨大的。

entries.definition: to pile up gradually, stressing slow increase.
entries.definitionCN: 逐渐累积，强调缓慢增加。

entries.definition: to amass and secretly store away, often selfishly.
entries.definitionCN: 积藏并私自储存，常含吝啬意味。

entries.definition: to accumulate a reserve supply for future use.

normalIntro.en: Remember amass through its two building blocks.
normalIntro.cn: 通过两个构件记住 amass。

normal.en: a- (to) + mass: to gather into one mass.
normal.cn: a-（朝向）+ mass（团块）：聚成一大团。

normal.en: Think of a snowball rolling downhill, adding mass as it goes.
normal.cn: 想想滚下山的雪球，一路越滚越大。

normal.en: Family chain: mass → massive → amass, from lump to huge to gathered-up.
normal.cn: 词族链：mass → massive → amass，从团块到巨大到聚集成堆。

normal.en: Amass usually implies quantity built over time, not a single act.
normal.cn: amass 通常指长期积累的量，而非一次动作。

normal.en: Common partners: fortune, wealth, data, troops, debts.
normal.cn: 常见搭配对象：财富、钱财、数据、军队、债务。

abstract.en: Picture coins sliding off a table into one heavy pile.
abstract.cn: 想象硬币从桌上滑落，堆成沉甸甸的一堆。

abstract.en: See dust settling layer upon layer on a quiet shelf.
abstract.cn: 看灰尘一层层落在安静的书架上。

abstract.en: Watch soldiers streaming in from all roads to one field.
abstract.cn: 看士兵从各条道路汇聚到同一片旷野。

examples.en: He amassed millions of followers within two years.
examples.cn: 他在两年内积累了数百万粉丝。

examples.en: The team amassed a huge body of research data.
examples.cn: 团队积累了庞大的研究数据。

examples.en: Clouds amassed on the horizon before the storm.

definition_zh: 业余爱好者；业余的；外行的
definition_en: a person who takes part in an activity for pleasure rather than for money, or someone lacking professional skill
core_image: 周末公园里，一群爱好者扛着相机拍鸟
scene: 社区球场上，一群下班后赶来的球员换上球衣，没有一个人拿报酬。The tournament is open to amateur players only.
sceneCN: 这里 amateur 是「业余的」（第 2 个义项：不以该项活动为职业、不取报酬）；句意是这项赛事只对业余选手开放。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：业余水平的；不够专业的
名词：业余主义；业余身份
形容词：爱情的，与 amateur 同源于拉丁语「爱」

senses.title: One who does it for love
senses.definition: a person who takes part in an activity for pleasure rather than as a job
senses.definitionCN: 出于兴趣而非职业参加某项活动的人
senses.example: He is a keen amateur photographer on weekends.
senses.exampleCN: 他周末是个热心的业余摄影爱好者。
senses.why: The word goes back to Latin amator, 'lover', so an amateur is literally someone who does the activity for the love of it rather than for pay.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可追溯到拉丁语 amator「爱者」，所以 amateur 字面上就是因热爱而做某件事的人，而不是为报酬而做。

senses.title: Not professional
senses.definition: describing sport, art, or work done outside a profession and usually without payment
senses.definitionCN: 形容在职业体系之外进行、通常没有报酬的运动、艺术或工作
senses.example: The tournament is open to amateur players only.
senses.exampleCN: 这项赛事只对业余选手开放。
senses.why: Once amateur names the person, it can describe the whole level of activity, setting it against the paid professional circuit.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 amateur 能指人，它也能形容整个活动层级，与有报酬的职业圈相对。

senses.title: A clumsy non-expert
senses.definition: a disapproving word for someone whose work shows lack of professional skill
senses.definitionCN: 带贬义，指工作显出缺乏专业训练的人
senses.example: The repairs were done by amateurs and soon fell apart.
senses.exampleCN: 这些维修是外行做的，很快就散架了。
senses.why: Because love without training can look clumsy, the word acquired a sneer: an amateur is not merely unpaid but unskilled.
senses.whyCN: 因为只有热爱而缺乏训练往往显得笨拙，这个词便带上讥讽：amateur 不只是没有报酬，还是技艺不精。

intro.en: Amateur is a love word: it descends from the Latin verb 'to love'.
intro.cn: amateur 是个与「爱」有关的词，源自拉丁语动词「爱」。

items.en: amare meant 'to love', the source of amatory and of amateur.
items.cn: amare 意为「爱」，是 amatory 与 amateur 的来源。

items.en: amator meant 'lover, one who loves', without any hint of incompetence.
items.cn: amator 意为「爱者、热爱者」，丝毫没有不专业的意思。

items.en: French amateur named someone who cultivates an art or sport for pleasure.
items.cn: 法语 amateur 指为兴趣而从事艺术或运动的人。

items.en: English adopted the word for the growing world of clubs, sports, and hobbies.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入该词，用于兴起的俱乐部、运动与爱好圈子。

items.en: The disapproving sense 'unskilled' developed alongside the neutral one, so context decides the tone.
items.cn: 贬义的「不熟练」与中性的「业余」并行发展，语气由语境决定。

note.en: The look-alike group grows from the same root; the near-meaning group contrasts levels of skill and pay.
note.cn: 形近组同出一源；近义组对比技艺与报酬的层级。

sensesIntro.en: Love of the activity yields three readings: the enthusiast, the unpaid level, and the unskilled outsider.

definition_zh: 使惊奇；使惊叹
definition_en: to surprise someone very much, often with something impressive or hard to believe
core_image: 观众仰头看着魔术师让整架钢琴凭空消失
scene: 魔术师把硬币从空中变出来，台下的孩子张大了嘴。The trick amazed the whole audience.
sceneCN: 这里 amaze 是「使惊奇」（第 1 个义项：因出乎意料或难以置信而使人震惊）；句意是这个魔术让全场观众惊叹。

senses.title: To surprise greatly
senses.definition: to surprise someone strongly with something unexpected
senses.definitionCN: 用出乎意料的事让人受到强烈震动
senses.example: The trick amazed the whole audience.
senses.exampleCN: 这个魔术让全场观众惊叹。
senses.why: The word began as a verb meaning to confuse or stupefy, so the core of amaze is not mild surprise but being mentally knocked off balance.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初意为「使困惑、使发懵」，所以 amaze 的核心不是轻微的意外，而是让人一时失去思考的平衡。

senses.title: To fill with wonder
senses.definition: to impress someone deeply with something beautiful, vast, or skilful
senses.definitionCN: 以美丽、宏大或技艺高超之物深深打动某人
senses.example: Her courage amazed everyone who knew her.
senses.exampleCN: 她的勇气让认识她的人都由衷赞叹。
senses.why: When the cause is admirable rather than merely unexpected, the same shock turns into wonder, which is why amazing often carries praise.
senses.whyCN: 当引起震动的对象不只是意外，而且令人钦佩时，同样的冲击就转为赞叹，所以 amazing 常带褒义。

intro.en: Amaze began as a word for mental confusion, and only later settled into wonder.
intro.cn: amaze 最初表示头脑混乱，后来才固定为惊叹。

items.en: amasian meant 'to confuse, to stupefy', formed with the prefix a- on a base related to maze.
items.cn: amasian 意为「使困惑、使发懵」，由前缀 a- 加与 maze 相关的词基构成。

items.en: The verb still meant 'to bewilder', with fear and confusion in the foreground.
items.cn: 这个动词仍意为「使迷惑」，恐惧与混乱是其重点。

items.en: Amaze shifted towards 'to overwhelm with wonder', losing most of its old sense of panic.
items.cn: 十六世纪 amaze 转向「以惊奇压倒人」，旧有的惊慌义大体消失。

items.en: Amazement and amazing grew alongside, and amazing later became a general adjective of praise.
items.cn: amazement 与 amazing 随之发展，amazing 后来成为泛用的褒义形容词。

items.en: Modern amaze is a strong but usually positive word, close to astonish but warmer.
items.cn: 现代 amaze 语气强烈但通常偏正面，接近 astonish 却更带温度。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the maze base; the near-meaning group grades the strength of surprise.
note.cn: 形近组共享 maze 词基；近义组按惊讶强度分级。

normal.en: A maze bewilders, and amaze once meant bewilder.
normal.cn: 迷宫使人迷失，amaze 曾经就意为使人迷失。

normal.en: Amazing is the adjective of praise.

normal.en: Be amazed at or by, not with.

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-MAZE.

abstract.cn: 想象舞台上凭空消失的钢琴。

abstract.en: See a child's mouth open at a magic trick.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子看魔术时张大的嘴。

abstract.en: Imagine a crowd silent for a second, then cheering.
abstract.cn: 想象全场静了一秒，随后欢呼。

examples.en: The speed of the recovery amazed the doctors.
examples.cn: 恢复的速度让医生们惊叹。

examples.en: We were amazed at how quiet the city felt at dawn.
examples.cn: 黎明时城市的安静让我们惊讶。

examples.en: Her ability to remember names never ceases to amaze me.
examples.cn: 她记名字的本领总让我惊叹。

dict_mnemonic.text: a 加 maze（迷宫）：把人带进迷宫，脑子转不出来，就是「使惊奇」。

root: 源自古英语 amasian「使困惑、使发懵」，由前缀 a- 加与 maze「迷宫」相关的词基构成；十六世纪起转向「以惊奇压倒人」，并派生出 amazement、amazing 等词。

sensesIntro.en: A shock to the mind can be mere surprise or admiring wonder, and the word covers both.
sensesIntro.cn: 对头脑的冲击可以是单纯的意外，也可以是钦佩的赞叹，这个词两者都包。

definition_zh: 大使；使节；（品牌或事业的）代表
definition_en: the senior diplomat sent by a country to another, or a person who represents a brand or cause
core_image: 大使馆门前，一位身着正装的人递交国书
scene: 新任大使在总统府递交国书，随后与当地官员握手寒暄。The new ambassador presented her credentials at the palace.
sceneCN: 这里 ambassador 是「大使」（第 1 个义项：一国派往另一国的最高外交代表）；句意是新任大使在总统府递交国书。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：大使的；大使级的
名词：女大使；大使夫人，旧用法
名词：大使馆；使馆全体人员

senses.title: A country's top diplomat
senses.definition: the senior official who represents one country's government in another country
senses.definitionCN: 一国政府派驻另一国的最高级别代表
senses.example: The new ambassador presented her credentials at the palace.
senses.exampleCN: 新任大使在总统府递交了国书。
senses.why: The word goes back to a medieval term for a mission or service, so an ambassador is the person sent to carry out that mission abroad.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可追溯到中世纪表示「使命、差事」的词，所以大使就是被派往国外执行这项使命的人。

senses.title: A representative of a brand or cause
senses.definition: a well-known person who publicly represents a company, charity, or idea
senses.definitionCN: 公开代表某公司、慈善机构或理念的知名人物
senses.example: The retired player became an ambassador for the children's charity.
senses.exampleCN: 这位退役球员成了该儿童慈善机构的代言人。
senses.why: A diplomat speaks for a country, and modern marketing borrowed that role: the brand ambassador speaks for a brand in public.
senses.whyCN: 外交官代表国家发声，现代营销借用了这个角色：品牌代言人在公众场合代表品牌。

intro.en: Ambassador came into English from French, and its deeper origin is a word for service or mission.
intro.cn: ambassador 经法语进入英语，更早的来源是表示「服务、使命」的词。

items.en: A Celtic word ambactus meant 'servant, retainer', and it passed into Latin.
items.cn: 凯尔特语 ambactus 意为「仆人、随从」，并传入拉丁语。

items.en: ambactia meant 'service, mission', the duty a retainer carried out.
items.cn: ambactia 意为「服务、使命」，即随从承担的任务。

items.en: French named the person who carried out such a mission, and English borrowed the form.
items.cn: 法语用 ambassadeur 指执行这类使命的人，英语借用了这一形式。

items.en: English ambassador first meant a messenger or representative of a ruler.
items.cn: 英语 ambassador 最初指君主的信使或代表。

items.en: The diplomatic sense became fixed, and the twentieth century added the brand ambassador.
items.cn: 外交义固定下来，二十世纪又增添了品牌代言人的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group is the embassy family; the near-meaning group ranks diplomatic roles.
note.cn: 形近组是使馆词族；近义组按外交职级排列。

definition_zh: 歧义；含糊；模棱两可；犹豫不决；（意图的）不确定
definition_en: the quality of having more than one possible meaning, of being unclear, or of a state of doubt in which the mind cannot settle
core_image: 一句话被同时驱向两条路：两种读法都站得住，谁也没被甩开
scene: 审稿人读到「他们给旧船刷了漆和发动机」这一句，先笑出声，随后在页边写下批注。The reviewer reads the sentence 'they painted the old boat and the engine', laughs, and notes the structural ambiguity in the margin.
sceneCN: 这里 ambiguity 是「句法歧义」（第 4 个义项：句子结构可作两种切分）；句意：审稿人读到这句话先笑出声，随后在页边记下它的句法歧义。场景要点：稿纸页边的批注、被圈出的 and、两种颜色的修改笔、停住的笔尖。

senses.title: Doubting, unable to decide
senses.titleCN: 犹疑不决：心智停不下来
senses.definition: the state of being unable to decide or of hesitating between possibilities
senses.definitionCN: 无法作出决定、在几种可能之间犹豫不定的状态
senses.example: His ambiguity about the job offer showed in the way he kept changing the subject.
senses.exampleCN: 他对这份工作邀请的犹豫，表现在他总把话题岔开。
senses.why: This is the earliest English sense, recorded c.1400. Latin ambigere meant 'to be driven around', so the mind here is not empty of meaning; it is pulled first one way and then the other.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语最早的义项，约记录于 1400 年。拉丁语 ambigere 意为“被驱赶着转来转去”，所以这里并非“没有意思”，而是心智先被拉向一边、又被拉向另一边。

senses.title: Two meanings in one word
senses.titleCN: 一词两义：同一个词被读出两种意思
senses.definition: the quality of a word or phrase that can be understood in two or more different ways
senses.definitionCN: 一个词或短语可以被理解成两种或多种不同意思的性质
senses.example: The ambiguity of 'bank' made the joke work.
senses.exampleCN: bank 一词的歧义让这个笑话成立了。
senses.why: Once ambiguity names the word rather than the mind, the two directions of ambigere become two readings of one form. The word itself is the crossroads where both roads stay open.
senses.whyCN: 当 ambiguity 指的不是心智而是词语时，ambigere 的两个方向就变成同一个词形的两种读法。词本身就是那个两条路都敞开的十字路口。

senses.title: The meaning is left unclear
senses.titleCN: 表述含混：意义没有被说清
senses.definition: the quality of a statement or description that is not precise enough to be understood clearly
senses.definitionCN: 陈述或描述不够精确、因而无法被清楚理解的性质
senses.example: Critics attacked the ambiguity of the policy statement.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者抨击那份政策声明的含混不清。
senses.why: Here the two readings are not both useful; the text simply fails to close the gap. The same fork remains, but it is now a defect of description, recorded from the early 15th century.
senses.whyCN: 这里两种读法并非都有用，文本只是没能把缺口合上。同一个分叉仍在，但此时它是表述上的缺陷；这一用法记录于 15 世纪早期。

senses.title: Two parses of one sentence
senses.titleCN: 同一句话的两种句法切分
senses.definition: in linguistics, the property of a sentence whose grammatical structure can be analysed in more than one way
senses.definitionCN: 在语言学中，指句子的语法结构可以被分析成不止一种形式
senses.example: The sentence 'old men and women' is famous for its structural ambiguity.
senses.exampleCN: “old men and women”这句话以结构歧义著称。
senses.why: The fork is no longer in the dictionary but in the brackets: [old men] and women assigns old to men only, while old [men and women] assigns it to both. One string of words supports two trees.
senses.whyCN: 分叉不在词典里，而在括号里：[old men] and women 把 old 只给 men，而 old [men and women] 把 old 同时给了 men 和 women。同一串词支撑起两棵句法树。

senses.title: Deliberate ambiguity in negotiation
senses.definition: the intentional use of unclear wording so that different parties can each read what they want into it
senses.definitionCN: 故意使用不清楚的措辞，让不同各方都能从中读出自己想要的意思
senses.example: The agreement preserved a deliberate ambiguity over the status of the region.
senses.exampleCN: 该协议在该地区的地位问题上保留了一种有意的含糊。
senses.why: Both readings are kept alive on purpose. Instead of driving the mind to a decision, the wording lets each side drive it in its own direction, so ambiguity becomes a diplomatic tool rather than a fault.
senses.whyCN: 两种读法被有意地同时保留。措辞不把心智驱向某个决定，而是让每一方把它驱向自己的方向，于是含糊从缺陷变成了外交工具。

senses.title: One picture, two figures
senses.definition: the quality of an image or sound that can be perceived in two different ways, as in an ambiguous figure
senses.definitionCN: 图像或声音可以被感知为两种不同样式的性质，如双义图形
senses.example: The duck-rabbit drawing is a classic case of perceptual ambiguity.
senses.exampleCN: 鸭兔图是知觉歧义的经典例子。
senses.why: The eye, like the mind in the earliest sense, is driven to two gestalts and can flip between them. Both readings are fully present in the same stimulus, so neither can be dismissed.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛就像最早义项里的心智，被驱向两种完形，并在两者之间翻转。两种读法都完整地存在于同一个刺激中，因此哪一种都无法被排除。

senses.title: An unclear position or role
senses.definition: the state of having a role or status that is not clearly defined, so that expectations remain unsettled
senses.definitionCN: 所担任的角色或地位没有被清楚界定、因而期待始终悬而未决的状态
senses.example: The ambiguity of her position as adviser and friend caused friction.
senses.exampleCN: 她既是顾问又是朋友，这种身份的模糊引发了摩擦。
senses.why: A person can occupy two categories at once. Neither label wins, so the social situation wavers like the original verb: the same person is legitimately read two ways.
senses.whyCN: 一个人可以同时占据两个类别。两个标签都不占上风，于是社会处境像原动词一样摇摆：同一个人被两种方式合理地解读。

senses.title: Meaning left open in a work
senses.titleCN: 作品中保留的开放意义
senses.definition: in literature and art, the quality of a work that invites several readings without settling on one
senses.definitionCN: 在文学与艺术中，作品邀请多种读法而不落定于其一的品质
senses.example: The ambiguity of the ending is what makes the novel memorable.
senses.exampleCN: 结局的开放含混正是这部小说令人难忘的原因。
senses.why: Here the fork is valued rather than repaired. The work holds two readings in suspension and leaves the reader to waver, turning the old defect into an aesthetic effect.
senses.whyCN: 这里的分叉是被珍视的，而不是被修复的。作品把两种读法悬置起来，让读者自己去摇摆，把旧的缺陷转成了审美效果。

senses.title: Unclear intention behind an act
senses.definition: the quality of an action or gesture whose underlying intention cannot be determined, even when the words or act themselves are clear
senses.definitionCN: 行为或姿态背后的意图无法确定，即使言语或动作本身很清楚
senses.example: There was an ambiguity in his kindness that made her distrust it.
senses.exampleCN: 他的善意里有某种说不清的意味，让她反而起了疑心。
senses.why: Two possible motives are driven at once, so the fork moves from wording to intention. The act is plain, but why it was done remains double, which is why the word can describe motives as well as sentences.
senses.whyCN: 两种可能的动机同时被驱动，分叉就从措辞移到了意图。行为本身很清楚，但“为什么这样做”仍然是双重的；因此这个词既能描述句子，也能描述动机。

intro.en: Ambiguity comes from Latin ambiguitas, a noun of state from ambiguus 'having double meaning'. The verb behind it is ambigere 'to dispute, wander, waver', literally ambi- 'about, both ways' + agere 'to drive'. The second element is therefore agere, not a piece that sounds like 'guity'; the core image is a mind driven in two directions at once.
intro.cn: ambiguity 来自拉丁语 ambiguitas，是由 ambiguus“有两种意思的”构成的状态名词。其背后的动词是 ambigere“争执、徘徊、犹豫”，字面为 ambi-“两边、周围”+ agere“驱动”。因此第二成分是 agere，而不是某个听起来像“guity”的部分；核心意象是心智同时被驱向两个方向。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'uncertainty, doubt, indecision, hesitation', from Old French ambiguite and directly from Latin ambiguitatem (nominative ambiguitas). The earliest sense is about the doubting mind, not about a double-meaning word.
items.cn: 英语最早记录为“不确定、怀疑、犹豫不决”，来自古法语 ambiguite，并直接来自拉丁语 ambiguitatem（主格 ambiguitas）。最早的义项说的是犹豫的心智，而不是一词两义。

items.en: Ambiguitas was a noun of state from ambiguus 'having double meaning, doubtful'. That adjective already contains the fork: a thing can be taken in two ways, and therefore the person facing it does not know which way to go.
items.cn: ambiguitas 是由 ambiguus“有两种意思的、可疑的”构成的状态名词。那个形容词本身已经含有分叉：一件事可以被两种方式理解，因此面对它的人不知道该往哪边走。

items.en: Ambigere meant 'to dispute about, contend, debate', but literally 'to wander, go about, go around', and figuratively 'to hesitate, waver, be in doubt'. The physical image is being driven around in circles rather than arriving at a point.
items.cn: ambigere 意为“就……争执、辩论”，但字面是“游荡、四处走、绕圈”，引申为“犹豫、摇摆、存疑”。其身体意象是被驱赶着绕圈，而不是抵达某一点。

items.en: Ambi- 'about' is from PIE *ambhi- 'around'; agere 'drive, lead, act' is from PIE *ag- 'to drive, draw out or forth, move'. So the word is built on driving, not on any root meaning 'doubt' or 'two-faced'. Ambiguity is what happens when something is driven both ways at once.
items.cn: ambi-“周围”来自原始印欧语 *ambhi-“环绕”；agere“驱动、引领、行动”来自 *ag-“驱赶、拉出、移动”。因此这个词建立在“驱动”上，而不是任何意为“怀疑”或“两面”的词根上。ambiguity 就是某物被同时驱向两边的结果。

items.en: The sense 'obscurity in description' is recorded from the early 15th century. The adjective ambiguous follows later, first attested in Sir Thomas More in 1528, so the abstract noun was in English before its adjective became common.
items.cn: “描述含混”这一义项记录于 15 世纪早期。形容词 ambiguous 出现更晚，最早见于 1528 年的托马斯·莫尔；也就是说，这个抽象名词先进入英语，其形容词后来才通行。

items.en: Modern English extends the same fork to syntax, perception, diplomacy, social roles, art and motive. Two look-alikes must be kept apart: ambivalent is ambi- + valere 'to be worth, be strong', and ambition is ambi- + ire 'to go'. Neither shares the agere element of ambiguity.
items.cn: 现代英语把同一个分叉扩展到句法、知觉、外交、社会角色、艺术与动机。两个形似词必须分开：ambivalent 是 ambi- + valere“有价值、有力量”，ambition 是 ambi- + ire“走”。两者都不含 ambiguity 的 agere 成分。

note.en: The first group separates words that look or sound like ambiguity but are built from different Latin verbs; the second compares words learners often use in its place. The key test is whether the trouble lies in two readings or in missing knowledge.
note.cn: 第一组区分那些形似或音似 ambiguity、却由不同拉丁动词构成的词；第二组比较学习者常用来替换它的词。关键区别是：麻烦究竟来自“两种读法”，还是来自“知识缺失”。

entries.definition: having more than one possible meaning. It is the adjective from ambiguity and names the thing that carries two readings, not the state of doubt itself.
entries.definitionCN: 具有不止一种可能意思的。它是 ambiguity 派生的形容词，指承载两种读法的那个东西，而不是犹疑状态本身。

entries.definition: having mixed or conflicting feelings about someone or something. It is ambi- plus Latin valere 'to be strong, be worth', so it is about two pulls of feeling, not two meanings.
entries.definitionCN: 对某人或某事怀有混合、矛盾的情感。它是 ambi- 加拉丁语 valere“有力量、有价值”，说的是两种情感拉力，而不是两种意思。

entries.definition: a strong desire to achieve something. It goes back to Latin ambire 'to go around', originally canvassing for votes: ambi- + ire 'to go', with no agere.
entries.definitionCN: 实现某事的强烈愿望。它上溯拉丁语 ambire“四处走”，原指为拉票而奔走：ambi- + ire“走”，不含 agere。

entries.definition: relating to walking, or able to walk. It comes from Latin ambulare 'to walk', which merely happens to begin with amb-. There is no ambi- prefix at all.
entries.definitionCN: 与行走有关的，或能行走的。它来自拉丁语 ambulare“行走”，只是碰巧以 amb- 开头，根本没有 ambi- 前缀。

entries.definition: the quality of being imprecise or lacking a clear boundary. Vagueness says the edges are fuzzy; ambiguity says two or more distinct readings are actually available.
entries.definitionCN: 不精确或缺少清晰边界的性质。vagueness 说边界模糊；ambiguity 说确实存在两种或更多彼此不同的读法。

entries.definition: the use of a word with more than one meaning in order to mislead. Equivocation adds the intent to deceive, while ambiguity can be innocent or even useful.
entries.definitionCN: 利用一词多义来误导他人。equivocation 多了一层欺骗意图，而 ambiguity 可以是无意的，甚至是有用的。

entries.definition: the state of not knowing what will happen or what is true. Uncertainty is about the observer's ignorance; ambiguity is about the object supporting several readings.
entries.definitionCN: 不知道会发生什么或什么是真的。uncertainty 说的是观察者的无知；ambiguity 说的是对象本身支持多种读法。

entries.definition: the quality of being hard to understand because it is hidden or unfamiliar. Obscurity hides one meaning; ambiguity displays two.
entries.definitionCN: 因隐蔽或陌生而难以理解的性质。obscurity 把一种意思藏起来；ambiguity 则把两种意思摆出来。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: ambi- 'both ways' plus agere 'to drive', the ambiguity family, and the three look-alikes built from valere, ire and ambulare.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：ambi-“两边”加 agere“驱动”、ambiguity 词族，以及由 valere、ire、ambulare 构成的三个形似词。

normal.en: ambi- means 'both ways' and agere means 'to drive'. Ambiguity is literally a thing driven in two directions at once.
normal.cn: ambi- 意为“两边”，agere 意为“驱动”。ambiguity 字面上就是“被同时驱向两边的状态”。

normal.en: The same agere root gives agent, act, agenda and agile, so ambiguity belongs with 'driving and doing', not with any word for 'two-faced'.
normal.cn: 同一 agere 词根给出 agent、act、agenda、agile，所以 ambiguity 属于“驱动与行动”这一族，与任何“两面”词无关。

normal.en: Three look-alikes use three different second elements: ambivalent has valere 'be worth', ambition has ire 'go', ambulatory has ambulare 'walk'.
normal.cn: 三个形似词用了三个不同的第二成分：ambivalent 是 valere“有价值”，ambition 是 ire“走”，ambulatory 是 ambulare“行走”。

normal.en: The earliest sense was 'hesitation', not 'double meaning'. The mind wavered first; the word's double meaning was named later.
normal.cn: 最早的义项是“犹豫”，不是“一词两义”。先有摇摆的心智，后来才用它命名词语的双重意思。

normal.en: Structural ambiguity lives in brackets: [old men] and women versus old [men and women].
normal.cn: 结构歧义活在括号里：[old men] and women 对 old [men and women]。

abstract.en: Picture a road that splits at a fork. The driver is not lost for lack of a map; both roads are real, and the car is pulled down each one in turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一条在岔口分开的路。司机并非因为没有地图而迷路；两条路都真实存在，车子被先后拉向每一条。

abstract.en: The same fork can sit in a word, a sentence, a drawing, a treaty, a job title or a gesture. What stays constant is that two readings remain standing at once.
abstract.cn: 同一个分叉可以藏在单词、句子、图画、条约、职位名称或一个姿态里。不变的是：两种读法同时立着。

abstract.en: Sometimes the fork is a fault to be repaired; sometimes it is deliberately preserved. Ambiguity can therefore be either a problem or a resource.
abstract.cn: 有时这个分叉是要修掉的缺陷，有时它被有意保留。因此 ambiguity 既可能是问题，也可能是资源。

examples.en: Please rewrite the sentence to remove its ambiguity.
examples.cn: 请改写这句话，消除它的歧义。

examples.en: The play ends in ambiguity, and each audience member decides what happened.
examples.cn: 这部剧以含糊收场，每位观众都自己判断到底发生了什么。

examples.en: There was an ambiguity in her tone that made him unsure whether she was joking.
examples.cn: 她的语气里有某种含混，让他拿不准她是不是在开玩笑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺必鬼题」——俺必答的那道鬼题，两个答案都说得通 → ambiguity 歧义、模棱两可

root: 来自拉丁语 ambiguitas，上溯 ambiguus“有两种意思的”与 ambigere“徘徊、争执”，字面是 ambi-“两边”加 agere“驱动”，核心是“心智被同时驱向两边”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of ambiguity, all one fork: a form, a situation or a mind is driven in two directions at once. Sometimes both readings are legitimate, sometimes the split is a defect, and sometimes it is deliberately preserved.
sensesIntro.cn: ambiguity 的九个义项都源于同一个分叉：一个词形、一种处境或一颗心智被同时驱向两个方向。有时两种读法都合法，有时分裂是缺陷，有时它被有意保留。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one form or situation driven down two roads at the same time.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个词形或处境被同时驱上两条路。

branches.en: INNER FORK: hesitation and unclear motive. The mind is pulled both ways before any wording is fixed.
branches.cn: 内在分叉：犹豫与动机不明。措辞尚未固定，心智先被拉向两边。

branches.en: CODE: one word or one sentence carries two readings, whether in the dictionary or in the brackets.
branches.cn: 代码层：一个词或一句话承载两种读法，无论在词典里还是在句法括号里。

branches.en: TEXT: vagueness is a fault and open-endedness is a virtue, but both leave meaning unresolved.
branches.cn: 文本层：含混是缺陷，开放是美德，但两者都让意义悬而未决。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONS: negotiators and social roles keep two readings alive, sometimes on purpose and sometimes by accident.
branches.cn: 制度层：谈判者与社会角色让两种读法同时存活，有时出于有意，有时出于无意。

branches.en: PERCEPTION: the eye flips between two figures held in one drawing.
branches.cn: 知觉层：眼睛在一张图里所持的两个形象之间翻转。

intro.en: Ambiguity is a Latin-derived noun whose parts are frozen: ambi- 'both ways' + agere 'to drive' + -ity. English adds only ordinary suffixes to the finished family. The -ity is not a meaning-bearing 'guity' chunk, and the whole word never meant 'two-faced'.
intro.cn: ambiguity 是拉丁来源的名词，其成分已经凝固：ambi-“两边”+ agere“驱动”+ -ity。英语只是在成品词族后加普通后缀。-ity 并不是一个带意义的“guity”部件，整个词也从来不是“两面派”的意思。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is ambigere 'to dispute, wander, waver', its adjective ambiguus 'double-meaning, doubtful', and agere 'to drive, lead, act'. The same agere yields agent, act, agenda and agile, while ambivalent and ambition belong to valere and ire respectively.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族包括 ambigere“争执、徘徊、犹豫”、其形容词 ambiguus“有两种意思的、可疑的”，以及 agere“驱动、引领、行动”。同一 agere 给出 agent、act、agenda、agile，而 ambivalent 与 ambition 分别属于 valere 和 ire。

items.structure: ambi- (both ways) + agere (to drive) + -ity (noun of state)
items.meaning: the state of being driven two ways, hence double meaning or doubt
items.meaningCN: 被驱向两边的状态，因而指歧义或犹疑（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The ambiguity of the clause delayed the signing.
items.exampleCN: 条款的歧义推迟了签署。

items.meaning: open to more than one interpretation
items.meaningCN: 可作不止一种解释的；有歧义的（-ous 构成形容词）
items.example: He gave an ambiguous answer and left the room.
items.exampleCN: 他给了个模棱两可的回答，然后离开了房间。

items.meaning: in a way that can be understood in more than one sense
items.meaningCN: 以含糊、可作多种理解的方式（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: She smiled ambiguously and said nothing.
items.exampleCN: 她含义不明地笑了笑，什么也没说。

items.meaningCN: 有歧义性；含糊（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: The ambiguousness of the title was intentional.
items.exampleCN: 标题的含混是有意为之。

items.meaningCN: 不含糊的；只有一种清楚意思的（un- 否定）
items.example: The instructions were short and unambiguous.

items.meaning: in a way that leaves no doubt
items.meaningCN: 毫不含糊地；明确无误地
items.example: The court ruled unambiguously in her favour.
items.exampleCN: 法院明确无误地判她胜诉。

items.structure: ambi- (both) + valere (to be worth, be strong) — a different root
items.meaning: having mixed feelings; not the same as having two meanings
items.meaningCN: 有矛盾情感的；与“两种意思”不同源（valere 有价值、有力量）
items.example: She felt ambivalent about moving abroad.
items.exampleCN: 她对移居国外心情矛盾。

items.meaning: the state of having conflicting feelings
items.meaningCN: 矛盾情感；正反情绪并存（-ence 构成状态名词）
items.example: His ambivalence made the decision harder.
items.exampleCN: 他的矛盾心理让决定更难做。

items.structure: ambi- (around) + ire (to go) — a different root
items.meaning: a strong drive to achieve something, originally 'going around' to canvass
items.meaningCN: 雄心；抱负（原指四处奔走拉票，与 agere 无关）
items.example: Her ambition was to lead the research team.
items.exampleCN: 她的抱负是领导这个研究团队。

items.structure: ambi- (around) + ire (to go) — a different root
items.meaning: the scope or boundary of something
items.meaningCN: 范围；界限（同 ambire 一族，与 agere 无关）
items.example: That question lies outside the ambit of the inquiry.
items.exampleCN: 那个问题不在调查范围之内。

latinEntries.meaning: to dispute, wander, waver, be in doubt

definition_zh: 模棱两可的；含糊不清的；有歧义的
definition_en: open to more than one interpretation; not clear or decided

scene: 老师批复只写了一个「好」，学生猜不出是称赞还是敷衍。The teacher's reply was so ambiguous that no one knew whether it was praise or dismissal.
sceneCN: 这里的 ambiguous 是「模棱两可的」（第 1 个义项：可作多种解释）；句意是老师的回复含糊其辞，没人知道是称赞还是敷衍。

derivatives.zh: 由 ambiguous 加后缀 -ity 构成，义为「歧义；模棱两可」
由 ambiguous 加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「含糊地；歧义地」
由否定前缀 un- 加 ambiguous 构成，义为「明确的、毫不含糊的」

senses.title: Having more than one possible meaning
senses.titleCN: 有歧义的；可作多种解释的
senses.definition: having or expressing more than one possible meaning, so the reader must guess
senses.definitionCN: 具有或表达出不止一种可能的含义，使读者不得不猜测
senses.example: The sentence is ambiguous without a comma.
senses.exampleCN: 没有逗号，这个句子就有歧义。
senses.why: Latin ambigere means to wander around; a meaning that wanders between two readings is ambiguous.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ambigere 意为「四处游走」；含义在两种解读之间游移不定，正是歧义的本义。

senses.title: Not clear or deliberate in intention
senses.titleCN: 含糊其辞的；意向不明的
senses.definition: not stating a position clearly, often on purpose to keep options open
senses.definitionCN: 不明说立场，常为了保留回旋余地而故意含糊
senses.example: The spokesman gave an ambiguous reply about the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 发言人对并购一事给了个含糊其辞的答复。
senses.why: When a speaker refuses to settle on one meaning, the wandering meaning becomes deliberate vagueness.
senses.whyCN: 当说话者不肯在一种含义上安定下来，「游移的含义」就变成了有意为之的含糊。

senses.title: Mixed in character or feeling
senses.titleCN: 难以定性的；正邪难辨的
senses.definition: having two opposite qualities at once, such as good and bad, so the moral reading is unclear
senses.definitionCN: 同时具有两种对立性质（如善与恶），使人难以作出单一评价
senses.example: The hero of the film is a morally ambiguous figure.
senses.exampleCN: 影片的主人公是个道德上难以定性的人物。
senses.why: If meaning can wander, so can judgment; a person of two faces lets the moral reading wander too.
senses.whyCN: 既然含义可以游移，评价也可以游移；具有两副面孔的人物让道德判断悬而未决。

intro.en: Ambiguous comes from Latin ambigere, to wander around, from ambi- both ways plus agere to drive.
intro.cn: ambiguous 来自拉丁语 ambigere「四处游走」，由 ambi-（两边）+ agere（驱动）构成。

items.en: The root *ag- meant to drive or move; *ambhi- meant around.
items.cn: 词根 *ag- 表示「驱动、移动」；*ambhi- 表示「周围、两边」。

items.en: Latin ambi- meant both ways, and ambigere meant to wander around or waver.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ambi- 表示「两边」，ambigere 表示「游走、摇摆」。

items.en: The adjective ambiguus described anything unsettled or open to two readings.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词 ambiguus 描述一切悬而未决、可作两解的事物。

items.en: English adopted ambiguous around 1520 for doubtful and uncertain statements.
items.cn: 英语约在 1520 年借入 ambiguous，用于表示可疑、不明确的表述。

items.en: The word now covers verbal ambiguity, deliberate vagueness, and morally mixed characters.
items.cn: 现代用法涵盖语言歧义、有意含糊以及道德上的正邪难辨。

note.en: Ambiguous overlaps with vague and equivocal, and opposes explicit and unambiguous.
note.cn: ambiguous 与 vague、equivocal 意义交错，与 explicit、unambiguous 相对。

entries.definition: able to use both hands equally well

entries.definition: not clear in shape or meaning
entries.definitionCN: 模糊的，强调轮廓或含义不清晰

entries.definition: open to two interpretations, often deceptively
entries.definitionCN: 歧义的、闪烁其词的，常含故意误导之意

entries.definition: not clearly expressed or easily understood
entries.definitionCN: 晦涩的、费解的，强调难以理解而非多义

entries.definition: stated clearly and in detail
entries.definitionCN: 明确的、清楚的，直接反义

entries.definition: having only one possible meaning
entries.definitionCN: 毫不含糊的，由 ambiguous 加否定前缀构成的反义

normalIntro.en: Hold the prefix ambi- plus the root of driving to keep ambiguous straight.
normalIntro.cn: 抓住前缀 ambi- 加上「驱动」词根，就能记住 ambiguous。

normal.en: ambi- means both ways, as in ambidextrous and ambivalent.
normal.cn: ambi- 表示「两边」，也见于 ambidextrous、ambivalent。

normal.en: agere means to drive; ambiguous meaning is driven two ways.

normal.en: the noun is ambiguity, with -ity ending.
normal.cn: 名词是 ambiguity，以 -ity 结尾。

normal.cn: unambiguous 用否定前缀封掉一个方向，只剩一种含义。

normal.en: ambivalent is about feelings, ambiguous about meanings.
normal.cn: ambivalent 说的是心情矛盾，ambiguous 说的是含义多解。

abstract.en: See a road sign pointing left and right at once, promising both directions.
abstract.cn: 想象一块同时指向左右的标牌，承诺两个方向。

abstract.en: Picture a diplomat smiling and saying nothing definite at a press conference.
abstract.cn: 想象发言人在发布会上微笑着却不给一句确定的话。

abstract.en: Feel a coin spinning on the table: neither heads nor tails while it turns.
abstract.cn: 感受旋转中的硬币：转动时既非正面也非反面。

examples.en: His ambiguous answer satisfied nobody.
examples.cn: 他模棱两可的回答谁也不满意。

examples.en: The word carry is ambiguous between transport and support.
examples.cn: carry 一词在「运输」和「支撑」之间有歧义。

examples.en: The contract was rewritten to remove every ambiguous clause.
examples.cn: 合同被重写，删去了所有含糊的条款。

sensesIntro.cn: 义项从「一语双关的多义」出发，经「故意含糊」，延伸到「正邪难辨的复杂品性」。

definition_zh: 雄心；抱负；野心；志向
definition_en: a strong desire to achieve something, or the particular goal that desire is aimed at
core_image: 登山者抬头望着远处的顶峰，脚下还有很长的路
scene: 她在日记里写下十年后的目标：开一家自己的诊所。Her ambition is to run her own clinic one day.
sceneCN: 这里 ambition 是「志向；抱负」（第 2 个义项：想要达成的具体目标）；句意是她的志向是有朝一日经营自己的诊所。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：有雄心的；野心勃勃的
名词：范围；界限，与 ambition 同为拉丁词根

senses.title: The drive to succeed
senses.definition: a strong inner desire to achieve success, power, or a high position
senses.definitionCN: 内心强烈地想要取得成就、权力或高位的愿望
senses.example: Her ambition drove her to study late into the night.
senses.exampleCN: 她的雄心驱使她学习到深夜。
senses.why: The Latin root meant 'a going around', the walk a candidate made to gather votes, so ambition began as the restless movement of someone seeking office.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「四处走动」，即候选人拉票时的奔走，所以 ambition 最初就是谋求职位者那种停不下来的行动。

senses.title: A specific goal
senses.definition: the particular thing a person strongly wants to achieve in life
senses.definitionCN: 一个人一生中强烈想要达成的具体事情
senses.example: Her ambition is to run her own clinic one day.
senses.exampleCN: 她的志向是有朝一日经营自己的诊所。
senses.why: Once the drive has an object, the word can name that object directly, which is why ambition can be followed by a to-infinitive or a noun.
senses.whyCN: 当这股冲劲有了对象，这个词就可以直接指那个对象，因此 ambition 后可接不定式或名词。

intro.en: Ambition began as a word for political canvassing, and it still carries a whiff of the campaign trail.
intro.cn: ambition 最初指政治拉票，至今仍带着竞选路上的气味。

items.en: ambire meant 'to go around', formed from amb- 'about' and ire 'to go'.
items.cn: ambire 意为「四处走动」，由 amb-「周围」与 ire「走」构成。

items.en: ambitio named the round of visits a candidate made to win votes.
items.cn: ambitio 指候选人为了拉票而进行的一轮走访。

items.en: Roman writers used ambitio for self-seeking and vote-chasing, giving the word its darker edge.
items.cn: 罗马作家用 ambitio 指钻营与拉票，赋予这个词阴暗的一面。

items.en: French softened the word into a general desire for honour or success.
items.cn: 法语把这个词软化为对荣誉或成功的普遍渴望。

items.en: English keeps both faces: ambition as admirable drive and ambition as self-serving greed.
items.cn: 英语保留了两副面孔：令人钦佩的进取心，以及自私的贪欲。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin base; the near-meaning group grades desire and goals.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁词基；近义组区分渴望与目标。

examples.cn: 他的志向是成为一名飞行员。

examples.en: She has the ambition and the discipline to finish the course.
examples.cn: 她有完成这门课程的雄心和自律。

sensesIntro.en: The word names both the restless drive and the object it aims at.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词既指那股停不下来的冲劲，也指它瞄准的目标。

definition_zh: 有雄心的；野心勃勃的；规模宏大的
definition_en: having a strong desire for success or achievement; requiring great effort
core_image: 盯着山顶不肯回头望的登山者
scene: 她刚毕业就计划三年内开十家分店。The ambitious young manager planned to open ten branch stores within three years.
sceneCN: 这里的 ambitious 是「有雄心的」（第 1 个义项：渴求成功）；句意是这位雄心勃勃的年轻经理计划三年内开出十家分店。

pos.zh: 有雄心的；野心勃勃的；宏大的

senses.title: Strongly desiring success
senses.definition: having a strong desire to achieve success, power, or a high position
senses.definitionCN: 强烈渴望取得成功、权力或高位
senses.example: An ambitious student, she aimed for the top law school.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个有雄心的学生，目标直指顶尖法学院。
senses.why: Ambire in Latin means to go around canvassing votes; the image of someone moving eagerly toward a goal became the desire to rise.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ambire 意为「四处奔走拉票」；那种朝着目标积极奔走的画面，固化成了「渴望向上爬」的词义。

senses.title: Demanding great effort or resources
senses.titleCN: 规模宏大的；需要巨大投入的
senses.definition: describing a plan or goal that is large in scale and hard to achieve
senses.definitionCN: 形容计划或目标规模宏大、实现难度高
senses.example: The bridge was the most ambitious engineering project of its age.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥是那个时代最宏大的工程项目。
senses.why: A person full of desire sets goals larger than ordinary ones; the word then transfers from the desiring person to the oversized goal.
senses.whyCN: 欲望强烈的人定的目标往往超出常规；词义便从「有欲望的人」转移到「超常的目标」上。

senses.title: Eager in a negative, self-seeking way
senses.titleCN: 野心勃勃的；不择手段的（贬义）
senses.definition: having so strong a desire for power or success that honesty or others' interests may be sacrificed
senses.definitionCN: 对权力或成功的渴望强烈到可能牺牲诚信或他人利益
senses.example: His ambitious scheming cost him old friends.
senses.exampleCN: 他野心勃勃的算计让他失去了老朋友。
senses.why: Canvassing for votes edges toward manipulation; desire pushed past fairness turns ambition into scheming.
senses.whyCN: 拉票本就带有操纵意味；欲望越过公平的界限，雄心便滑向「钻营算计」的贬义。

intro.en: Ambitious comes from Latin ambire, to go around, the image of Roman candidates canvassing for votes.
intro.cn: ambitious 源于拉丁语 ambire「四处奔走」，其意象正是罗马候选人四处拉票。

items.en: The roots *ambhi- around and *eigh- to move combine in the sense of going about.
items.cn: 词根 *ambhi-（周围）与 *eigh-（移动）组合成「四处走动」之义。

items.en: Latin ambire meant to go around; ambitio meant a canvassing for office.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ambire 意为「四处走动」；ambitio 特指谋求官职时的拉票活动。

items.en: Old French ambicion kept the sense of desire for rank.
items.cn: 古法语 ambicion 保留了对位分的渴求之义。

items.en: English ambition first meant eager striving for honor, often with a negative shade.
items.cn: 英语 ambition 最初指对荣誉的急切追逐，常带贬义。

items.en: The adjective ambitious now praises drive as often as it warns against greed, and also describes huge undertakings.
items.cn: 现代形容词 ambitious 既赞许进取心也警示贪欲，还可形容规模浩大的事业。

note.en: Ambitious stands between aspiring and grasping, and pairs with its noun ambition.
note.cn: ambitious 介于褒义的 aspiring 与贬义的 grasping 之间，与其名词 ambition 配套。

intro.cn: ambitious 由 ambi-（周围）、表移动的 ire 词根和形容词后缀 -ous 组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin ambire and ambitio carry the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ambire 与 ambitio 支撑起整个词族。

definition_zh: 救护车；急救运输服务
definition_en: a vehicle that takes sick or injured people to hospital, or the emergency service that runs it
core_image: 闪着蓝灯的白色车辆穿过拥堵的街道
scene: 有人倒在路边，路人立刻拨打电话叫救护车。Someone called an ambulance as soon as the man collapsed.
sceneCN: 这里 ambulance 是「救护车」（第 1 个义项：运送伤病者去医院的车辆）；句意是那人一倒下，就有人叫了救护车。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：可走动的；门诊的，与 ambulance 同源
名词：救护车司机；急救员
动词：漫步，与 ambulance 同源于拉丁语「走」

senses.title: The emergency vehicle
senses.definition: a vehicle equipped to carry sick or injured people to hospital, often with flashing lights and a siren
senses.definitionCN: 装有急救设备、把伤病者送往医院的车辆，常带闪灯与警笛
senses.example: Someone called an ambulance as soon as the man collapsed.
senses.exampleCN: 那人一倒下，就有人叫了救护车。
senses.why: The word began as French hôpital ambulant, a 'walking hospital', and the vehicle inherited that name because treatment could move with the patient.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是法语 hôpital ambulant「行走的医院」，车辆沿用了这个名字，因为治疗可以随病人一起移动。

senses.title: The emergency service
senses.definition: the organised service, staff, and vehicles that respond to medical emergencies
senses.definitionCN: 应对医疗急症的有组织服务、人员与车辆体系
senses.example: The ambulance service in the region is short of staff.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的急救服务人手不足。
senses.why: Once the vehicle became familiar, the same noun could name the whole system that dispatches it, especially in phrases such as ambulance service.
senses.whyCN: 当这种车辆变得常见之后，同一个名词也能指调度它的整套体系，尤其在 ambulance service 这类短语里。

intro.en: Ambulance began as a moving hospital, and the Latin verb inside it simply means 'to walk'.
intro.cn: ambulance 最初指会移动的医院，其中的拉丁动词本义就是「走」。

items.en: ambulare meant 'to walk, to move about', the source of amble and ambulatory.
items.cn: ambulare 意为「走、四处移动」，是 amble 与 ambulatory 的来源。

items.en: French field hospitals were called hôpital ambulant, a hospital that moved with the army.
items.cn: 法语把随军移动的野战医院称为 hôpital ambulant。

items.en: The phrase shortened to ambulance, naming the mobile medical unit itself.
items.cn: 这一短语缩为 ambulance，用来指移动医疗单位本身。

items.en: Nineteenth-century military medicine made the word known across Europe.
items.cn: 十九世纪的军事医学使这个词在全欧洲为人所知。

items.en: In civilian use ambulance came to mean the vehicle that rushes patients to hospital.
items.cn: 在民用领域，ambulance 逐渐指把病人紧急送往医院的车辆。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin verb for walking; the near-meaning group names emergency responders.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「走」的动词；近义组列出急救相关角色。

entries.definition: able to walk, or relating to walking patients
to walk at a relaxed pace
moving from place to place
a person trained to give emergency medical care
any vehicle used in an emergency
a frame for carrying a sick person

normalIntro.en: Ambulance is a walking hospital: ambula means walk.
normalIntro.cn: ambulance 是会走路的医院：ambula 意为走。

normal.en: Latin ambulare means to walk.
normal.cn: 拉丁 ambulare 意为走。

normal.en: Amble is the same root at a slow pace.
normal.cn: amble 同根，指慢步走。

normal.en: Call an ambulance is the fixed emergency phrase.
normal.cn: call an ambulance 是固定的急救说法。

normal.en: Ambulance service means the whole system.
normal.cn: ambulance service 指整套急救体系。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AM-bu-lance.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AM-bu-lance。

abstract.en: Picture blue lights moving through traffic.
abstract.cn: 想象蓝灯穿过车流。

abstract.en: See a stretcher wheeled into a doorway.
abstract.cn: 想象担架被推进门口。

abstract.en: Hear a siren far off and getting closer.
abstract.cn: 听到远处渐近的警笛。

examples.en: The ambulance arrived within five minutes.
examples.cn: 救护车在五分钟内赶到了。

examples.en: He was taken to hospital by ambulance.
examples.cn: 他被救护车送往医院。

examples.en: Rural areas often rely on an air ambulance.
examples.cn: 农村地区常常依靠空中救护。

dict_mnemonic.text: ambul 意为「走」，-ance 是名词词尾：会走动的医院，就是救护车。

root: 源自拉丁语 ambulare「走、移动」，法语把随军移动的野战医院称为 hôpital ambulant，缩为 ambulance；十九世纪军事医学使其广为人知，民用后专指急送病人的车辆，并引申指急救服务体系。

sensesIntro.en: The moving hospital gave its name first to the vehicle and then to the service that runs it.
sensesIntro.cn: 「会移动的医院」先把名字给了车辆，再给了运营它的服务体系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white van with blue lights cutting through traffic.
core.cn: 核心意象：闪着蓝灯穿过车流的白色车辆。

a patient rushed to hospital
an air ambulance over mountains
a regional ambulance service
